your_book:
Jaleel's book had a broadly positive Monday, September 21, though it remains in the red overall at –1.19% unrealized. The loudest mover was Rocket Lab (RKLB), which surged +8.27% on the day — likely catching a bid from general market optimism around geopolitical headlines and futures strength. That single-session pop is eye-catching, but the position carries an AVOID verdict and a QARP score of just 38, the weakest in the book by a wide margin. The chip cohort also had a solid day: NVDA (+2.30%, ~10.3% weight) rode sector tailwinds from Intel/SK Hynix manufacturing talks and falling yields, while AVGO added +1.58%. Danaher (+2.03%) and Lululemon (+2.90%) were quiet contributors. AZO was the lone meaningful drag, slipping –1.80% with no clear catalyst beyond a broad consumer-spending narrative weighing on the name.

The sharpest drift in the book remains LULU: up +2.90% today but still sitting –21.1% in the hole, with a guidance cut flagged as elevated risk and Americas comps down five quarters running. BSX tells a similar story — a STRONG BUY verdict and an 80.3 QARP score, yet –10.8% unrealized and a slashed FY26 growth outlook with management guiding flat through Q3. The model likes both; the market hasn't agreed for some time. ONON (–13.0%), NBIX (–11.6%), and NVS (–13.2%) are also sitting well offside despite strong verdicts — these are the positions where the thesis and price action are most visibly diverging.

Watch ADBE into year-end: today's +0.21% came partly from AI-exec comments suggesting sector growth may slow, which temporarily softens the disruption narrative, but the CFO exit and AI-moat overhang haven't resolved. NBIX was the only name to move meaningfully against the tape today (–1.44%), notable given its elevated QARP of 82.4. The drug-pricing policy overhang across GILD, NVS, NBIX, and VRTX remains a slow-burn risk the book hasn't fully priced.
